headline: The powerful cold front was nearly out of LA County by late Thursday morning after very heavy rain and gusty winds, leaving scattered showers this afternoon and evening, then cool, dry weather Friday through most of the weekend.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The storm lived up to expectations: a very strong cold front swept the entire area with very heavy rain and gusty winds, including a peak of 2.26 inches in one hour in the San Fernando Valley near the Encino Reservoir, with storm totals of 1–3 inches along the coast and foothills and 2–5 inches on south-facing mountain slopes. As of 9:30 AM Thursday the front was close to leaving LA County, with periods of heavy rain around Glendale and the rest of the county for about another hour, then just scattered, mostly light to moderate showers into the evening with little added impact. Flood Watches run until 1, 3 or 6 PM depending on the area, Wind Advisories for south winds of 35–50 mph last until 1 or 4 PM, and LA County has a 20% chance of a thunderstorm until about 4 PM. Highs only reach the mid 60s, and 3–6 inches of snow may fall mostly above 7,000 feet late in the storm, too high to cause much trouble.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday turns dry, blustery and cool behind the storm, with fast northwest winds aloft and highs only in the low to mid 60s. A small area of high pressure brings a sunny Saturday, but highs rise just a degree or two and stay 4–8 degrees below normal. Dry weather continues through most of the weekend.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A minor disturbance brings a 20–30% chance of rain Sunday into Sunday night, with any amounts under two tenths of an inch, and computer models keep trending weaker; highs stay in the mid 60s. Monday is dry and mostly sunny and still 4–8 degrees below normal, and weak land-to-sea (offshore) flow Tuesday warms things 2–3 degrees into the mid to upper 60s without much wind. The next storm likely brings rain to the Central Coast Tuesday night or Wednesday but only a 30–40% chance south of Point Conception, including LA County, with at most about a half inch; models still disagree, and Thanksgiving Day looks dry for now.

coast: Dangerous beach conditions continue into Friday, peaking Thursday, with High Surf Advisories for all beaches: large surf brings very dangerous rip currents and hazardous jetties. Minor to moderate coastal flooding is possible, especially at high tide, with seawater over low-lying beaches, walkways and parking lots and significant beach erosion; the Central Coast could see localized wave damage (especially to piers), flooded roads and possibly structures, and large breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor (less so Ventura Harbor), with a Coastal Flood Advisory there Thursday. Offshore, ocean conditions stay dangerous through Friday with gusty winds and large seas, Small Craft Advisories into Friday, and a chance of thunderstorms over the water; winds turn northwest behind the front with showers possibly lingering into Friday, conditions improve Friday and turn fairly mild Saturday, and a weak front Sunday into Monday should have little impact. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides arrive Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day), and with more swells increasingly likely they will probably cause at least widespread moderate coastal flooding on all coasts, possibly significant if a larger swell lines up with the tides.
watch_for: Lingering flooding on streets and in flood-prone areas until Flood Watches expire this afternoon and evening, plus a 20% thunderstorm chance in LA County until about 4 PM.
Whether the Tuesday night–Wednesday storm reaches LA County (30–40% chance) ahead of Thanksgiving.
Record-high tides Thanksgiving week combined with new swells, raising the risk of widespread coastal flooding.
confidence: Forecasters are confident the worst of the storm is ending and in dry weather Friday through Monday, but have low confidence in the Tuesday night–Wednesday storm because computer models disagree.
